verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents a full REST API with a toggle-feature endpoint and an official MCP server that calls that API, and a hands-on probe created a flag through the API. For governance, it documents draft revisions with required approval before publishing, and its API docs say 'Require confirmation' holds risky changes until a person confirms them. missing for 10: explicit documentation that API/MCP flag writes are routed into approval drafts rather than published directly, any official CLI, independent or hands-on corroboration of approval enforcement on agent writes, and clarity on tier gating (approval workflows are listed only on the top pricing tier).

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: automate it (for example, from a deploy script) with the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
The official GrowthBook MCP server is a thin bridge: it loads GrowthBook Agent Skills (workflows and guardrails) and makes authenticated calls to the GrowthBook REST API.
Draft feature revisions, request review, resolve merge conflicts, and require approval before publishing.
Require confirmation holds risky changes until a person confirms them in GrowthBook.
